title: Spas Yogurt Soup
description: A soup made almost entirely of yogurt, held together with an egg and a spoonful of flour so it never splits, with barley for body and a spoon of mint butter stirred in at the end. Good hot in winter and cold in summer.
notes: Cold yogurt straight from the fridge is the usual cause of a curdled pot. Leave it out while the barley cooks and the tempering becomes almost foolproof.

steps.text: Simmer the pearl barley in the water until the grains are tender and have split slightly, then leave it in its cooking liquid.
Whisk the yogurt, egg and flour together in a large bowl until there is not a streak of flour left anywhere.
steps.tip: The egg and the flour are both insurance against splitting. Neither one alone is reliable in a pot this thin.

steps.text: Ladle a cupful of the hot barley liquid into the yogurt while whisking hard, then a second, then a third. The bowl should feel warm rather than hot before it goes anywhere near the stove.
steps.tip: Going the other way — yogurt into the pot — is how it curdles. Always bring the hot to the cool.

steps.text: Pour the tempered mixture back into the pot and bring it up to the laziest simmer, stirring in one direction the whole time. Never let it reach a rolling boil.
Meanwhile soften the onion in the butter in a small pan, then take it off the heat and stir in the dried mint.
steps.tip: Mint added to a hot pan goes dusty and grey. Off the heat it stays green and smells like mint.

steps.text: Stir the mint butter through the soup, season with the salt, and finish each bowl with cilantro.
